Chaque coup reçoit le même nombre de par: Every move gets the same number of games: the loop goes through all of them on each round. As they all have the same number of games, comparing the totals amounts to comparing the averages. The work is shared very well between the processor's cores: each thread plays its own games, and the totals are added up at the end.
La moyenne de N parties au hasard est un: The average of N random games is an estimate of the « random value » of the move, with an error that shrinks like 1/√N: four times more games, half the error. Without any knowledge of the game, the program thus discovers that shutting in its own pieces is bad: the random games that follow go wrong.
L'estimation de Monte Carlo répond à la: The Monte Carlo estimate answers the question « what is this move worth if everyone then plays at random? ». That is not the right question: the opponent does not play at random.
Un coup peut être excellent dans la plup: A move can be excellent in most continuations and losing against the only good reply. The average finds it good; an opponent who finds the reply punishes it.
Le temps est réparti également entre tou: The time is shared equally between all moves, including obviously bad ones.

Les deux défauts suivants sont corrigés: The last two flaws are fixed by MCTS (the next AI): focus the games on the promising moves, and build a tree so that the following moves are chosen too, not drawn at random.
MCTS garde les parties au hasard de Mont: MCTS keeps the random games of Monte Carlo, but builds in memory a tree of the positions already visited. Each node remembers two numbers: how many games went through it (n) and how many of them were won (w). The tree grows where it should: towards the promising moves, without quite abandoning the others.

Le coup joué est le plus visité, pas cel: The move played is the most visited one, not the one with the best win rate: a move tried 3 times and won 3 times is not reliable. The number of visits measures the confidence the search has given to the move.
Dans l'application, plusieurs threads pa: In the application, several threads share the same tree. So that they do not all go down the same path, a thread passing through a node temporarily adds a « virtual loss » to it: the node looks a little worse to the others, who explore other ones.
Au moment de la sélection, il faut un co: At selection time, a compromise is needed between exploitation (going down where we win the most) and exploration (checking the moves tried little, which may be underestimated). It is the multi-armed bandit problem: facing several slot machines, which one should you try?

Le terme d'exploration grandit lentement: The exploration term grows slowly (ln N) for everyone, and shrinks fast (1/nᵢ) for the child being visited: a neglected move is always visited again in the end.
Avec le temps, la proportion de visites: Over time, the share of visits to the bad moves tends to zero: the search converges to the best move (to the minimax, if it runs long enough).
Au tour de l'adversaire, le taux de vict: On the opponent's turn, the win rate is taken from their point of view: each side chooses what is good for them.

Le minimax suppose que l'adversaire joue: Minimax assumes the opponent plays perfectly. We expand the tree of all possible moves down to a certain depth. At the leaves, we evaluate the position with a number, the larger the better the position is for me. Then we go back up: on my turn, I take the maximum of the children; on theirs, they take the minimum.

Si le meilleur coup est examiné en premi: If the best move is examined first, the cut-offs come right away. In the best case, alpha-beta examines only about b^(d/2) leaves instead of b^d (b moves per position, depth d): for the same time, we go almost twice as deep. In the worst case (moves examined from worst to best), we gain nothing.

À la profondeur maximale, la partie n'es: At the maximum depth, the game is not over: we need an evaluation function that estimates who is ahead. The basic minimax's one is written by hand: a weighted sum of features of the position, computed for each side.
Quatre des caractéristiques mesurées sur: Four of the features measured on a real position: mobility, the squares reached first, the free squares around the pieces, the blocked pieces. The heuristic counts others (connectivity, isolated zones) and gives each one a different weight in the opening, the middle game and the endgame.

Les minimax NNUE reprennent l'alpha-bêta: The NNUE minimaxes take up alpha-beta as negamax, with the techniques of today's chess programs. Three of them change everything.
On cherche à profondeur 1, puis 2, puis: We search at depth 1, then 2, then 3, etc., until the allotted time runs out. We play the best move of the last completed depth. Redoing the small depths costs almost nothing (the last iteration dominates the cost), and each iteration gives the next one its best move, which it tries first: the move ordering improves.
Le nombre de nœuds est multiplié à chaqu: The number of nodes is multiplied at each depth (logarithmic scale). When time is up, the current iteration is abandoned.
Une même position peut être atteinte par: The same position can be reached by different move orders. A hash table (Zobrist key: an XOR of random numbers, one per piece and per square, updated at each move) remembers for each position already searched its value, the depth of the search, the type of bound (exact, at least, at most) and the best move. If the position comes back, we reuse the result, or at least the move, to try it first.

NNUE (Efficiently Updatable Neural Netwo: NNUE (Efficiently Updatable Neural Network, invented for shogi by Yu Nasu in 2018, then adopted by Stockfish) is a neural network designed to be evaluated millions of times per second in an alpha-beta search, on an ordinary processor.

Its result, before activation, is the sum of the weight columns of the active inputs: it is called the accumulator. A move switches only three inputs on or off (the piece leaves, the piece arrives, a hole appears): the accumulator is updated with three columns instead of recomputing everything. The following layers are tiny (1024 → 64 → 32 → 1).

So the dev first tries to prove the result (win, draw or loss), within part of the thinking time.

Avec plusieurs threads, chacun lance le: With several threads, each one runs the same iterative deepening on the same root. They share only the transposition table: what one thread proves, the others find in the table. As their move orders differ a little (and some skip depths), they explore different parts of the tree. Simple, lock-free, and effective.

The same pattern is thus learnt only once for both sides. Two accumulators (my view, their view) are kept up to date in parallel.

Les IA MCTS ResNet et AlphaZero utilisen: The MCTS ResNet and AlphaZero AIs use a completely different network: a deep convolutional network, like those that recognise images. The board is an image of 8 × 8 pixels with several channels (my pieces, their pieces, holes...).
Une convolution applique le même petit f: A convolution applies the same small 3 × 3 filter to each square: it detects a local pattern, wherever it is. By stacking layers, the network sees larger and larger patterns.
Le réseau empile 30 blocs de 256 filtres: The network stacks 30 blocks of 256 filters. Each block computes x + F(x): its input plus a correction. This shortcut (He et al., 2015) lets the information and the gradient through the 60 convolution layers, which makes it possible to train such a deep network.
La politique : une probabilité pour chaq: The policy: a probability for each move, « the move a good player would play here ».
La valeur : un nombre entre −1 et 1, « q: The value: a number between −1 and 1, « who is going to win from this position ».
Ce réseau fait plus de deux milliards de: This network does more than two billion multiply-adds per position (256 × 256 × 9 × 64 squares × 60 convolutions): on a graphics card (GPU), it evaluates tens of thousands per second; on the processor alone, far fewer. In the application, the MCTS uses the GPU with libtorch when it is available.

AlphaZero n'a besoin d'aucune partie hum: AlphaZero needs no human game and no expert: it plays against itself. Each move of these games is chosen by an MCTS search with the current network. The search is stronger than the network alone: the distribution of the root's visits is a better policy than the network's output. So the network is trained to predict these visits (policy) and the result of the game (value). The new network makes the search stronger, which produces better games, and so on.

Le minimax basique cherche à une profond: The basic minimax searches to a fixed depth. This one is given a time per move. A second thread acts as a clock: it sleeps for that time, then raises a « stop » flag. Meanwhile, the search does iterative deepening: depth 1, then 2, then 3, and so on up to 63. When the flag is raised, the current iteration is abandoned and the AI plays the best move of the last completed depth.

Chaque position cherchée est rangée dans: Each position searched is stored in a hash table (Zobrist key) with its value, the depth of the search, the type of bound (exact, at least, at most) and the best move found. If the position comes back, through another move order or at the next iteration, the table gives the value without searching, or at least narrows the window [α, β]. Even the leaves are stored, with the heuristic's value. The table size can be set (the « Settings » button).

Avec un bon ordre, le meilleur coup est: With a good ordering, the best move is almost always among the first. So the first two moves of each node are searched at full depth; the following ones first with 3 plies less. If this reduced search shows that the move does not beat α, it is dropped. Otherwise, it is searched again at full depth.

Pour utiliser plusieurs cœurs, la méthod: To use several cores, the method is deliberately lazy: each thread runs exactly the same search, from start to finish, with its own killer moves. They share only the transposition table. As they do not go at the same pace, the results one of them stores in the table save the others work, and each ends up exploring a little differently. At the end, the AI plays the move of the thread that completed the greatest depth.

Une partie au hasard est un signal très: A random game is a very noisy signal: good moves lose, bad moves win, because the rest is played any old way. The network learnt on well-played games: its estimate is much more reliable.
Une évaluation donne une valeur nuancée: An evaluation gives a nuanced value (for example 0.62), whereas a random game only gives won, drawn or lost.

Here, each leaf is an isolated position: the accumulator is recomputed entirely, about twenty columns of 1024 weights, then the small layers. It is still faster than a random game to the end. As in MCTS, a node is only expanded after 8 visits, which keeps the tree small in memory.
C'est l'idée d'AlphaZero, en plus simple: It is the idea of AlphaZero, made simpler: a network judges the leaves of an MCTS tree. AlphaZero goes further: its network also proposes the moves to try (the policy), and the PUCT formula replaces UCT. Compare with the « PUCT » chapter of MCTS ResNet.

Le bon minimax joue contre lui-même sur: The good minimax plays against itself on the cluster, 1 s per move on 9 cores. So that the games don't look alike, the first 2 to 9 moves are drawn at random (the file games_5r_1s holds the games with 5 random moves and 1 second per move). Each batch has about 75,000 games, and the board's symmetries multiply the positions further.
Octobre 2024 à mai 2025 : le premier NNU: October 2024 to May 2025: the first NNUE
Un premier réseau est appris en PyTorch: A first network is learnt in PyTorch on these games: from the position (193 inputs), it predicts whether the game ends in a win, a draw or a loss. It is rewritten in C++ in February 2025, sped up (vectorised matrix-vector products), then quantised in 8-bit integers between March and May 2025. In May 2025, a tournament on the cluster, 1000 return matches per pair, ranks all the AIs.
D'août à décembre 2025, c'est le minimax: From August to December 2025, it is the quantised NNUE minimax, now the best AI, that plays against itself: 2 s per move on 8 cores, in a new file format. An NNUE is retrained on these games. The first attempt is bad (« the new neural network is bad », November 2025: the weights were no longer bounded during training); it is fixed in December. Its gain in strength was not clearly established, but its games are used for everything that follows. In December 2025, the first NNUE is also used to judge the leaves of an MCTS tree instead of random games: that is MCTS NNUE.
Mars-avril 2026 : le réseau de features,: March-April 2026: the feature network, which reads computed features instead of the squares. Some features were proposed by a language model (Qwen) in an automatic loop; a « certain win » input was added.
Mai 2026 : le ResNet, un réseau convolut: May 2026: the ResNet, a residual convolutional network in the AlphaZero style (30 blocks of 256 filters, a value head and a moves head), learnt in a supervised way on the NNUE minimax's games, on several GPUs.
Juillet 2026 : la distillation. Le ResNe: July 2026: distillation. The ResNet, too slow for a minimax, becomes the teacher: it labels hundreds of millions of positions, and two small fast networks learn to imitate it. They are the ones that play in the application: Minimax NNUE (old), with 193 inputs, and Minimax Features, with 119 features.
Septembre 2026 : AlphaZero part du ResNe: September 2026: AlphaZero starts from the ResNet and improves by playing against itself, with a KataGo-style search, on the cluster's GPUs.
Octobre 2026 : le réseau d'AlphaZero dev: October 2026: AlphaZero's network becomes the teacher in turn. It labels about a billion positions, and the side-to-move NNUE of Minimax NNUE dev is distilled from it. The dev's search is reworked step by step, each idea measured over thousands of games.
Novembre 2026 : la boucle de distillatio: November 2026: the distillation loop. The dev's games are labelled, they improve the ResNet, which teaches the next NNUE. In the endgame (22 free squares or fewer), the target becomes the exact result, more reliable than the teacher.
La leçon : en IA des jeux, les données c: The lesson: in game AI, data matter as much as the algorithm. A slightly better AI produces better games, which train a better network, which gives an even better AI.
Les pistes qui n'ont pas abouti: The leads that did not pan out
Le journal du projet garde aussi les ess: The project's log also keeps the abandoned attempts. They cost as much work as the successes and taught as much: each was measured, then dropped on the numbers.
Juin 2024 : après les premières rondes d: June 2024: after the first rounds of the cross-entropy method, the Nelder-Mead method (a simplex that deforms in the weight space) was tried to improve the heuristic's weights further. It brought nothing, and the cross-entropy method was kept.
Juillet-août 2025 : un réseau logique au: July-August 2025: a logic network instead of a neural network. Each neuron is a gate with two inputs, which can be any of the 16 possible Boolean functions (AND, OR, exclusive OR, implication…). The output counts the gates switched on in three groups: Black wins, draw, White wins. The first attempt hands the choice of gates to the SMT solver z3: each gate is an unknown of 4 bits, and each training position adds a full copy of the circuit and the constraint « the right group wins ». The problem grows with each position, whereas a network learns from millions: z3 runs out of memory and returns no result. The second attempt searches for the gates and their connections with a genetic algorithm in C++ (August 2025). The lead was then dropped in favour of the NNUE, which learns by gradient descent.
Octobre 2026 : le coup nul (passer son t: October 2026: the null move (passing to see whether the position remains too good), a classic chess technique, costs Yolah 81 Elo. The « proxy cut » replaces it with a real ordinary move, deliberately weak, and gains 47 to 59 Elo. A paper was planned. It was abandoned when the same idea, tried in Stockfish and in other games, brought nothing clear.
Octobre 2026 : remplacer le NNUE, dans c: October 2026: replacing the NNUE, in some phases of the game, with a very fast learnt function (weighted bit counts). It errs 1.3 to 3.5 times more than the network, and is only better with seven free squares or fewer, where the search sees the end anyway.
Octobre 2026 : des tables d'ordre des co: October 2026: move-ordering tables learnt in advance, from the cut-offs observed in millions of positions. No effect when used to initialise the history (a game's « warm » history already does the job). They cost 16 to 25 Elo when their best moves are tried first.
Octobre 2026 : chercher automatiquement: October 2026: automatically searching for new NNUE features by generating programs. A small language of operations on bitboards (neighbours, queen range, closure, growth loops) produces programs, each scored on how much of the network's error it explains, with a penalty for its computing time. In 23 hours on the cluster, 9,073 programs were tried. The search found influence on its own, already known, but nothing new and cheap, apart from « the number of my pieces that can still move ».
Octobre 2026 : de nombreuses caractérist: October 2026: many space features given to the NNUE (corrected flood fill, queen distance, zones reached first, connectivity…). The most complete version has the best validation error, but loses 60 Elo in games: it costs too much to compute. An ablation over 92 columns confirmed that a small selection was enough.
Octobre 2026 : des statistiques de motif: October 2026: statistics of local patterns (3×3 and 5×5 around a piece) over 4.8 million games. They mostly measure mobility, which the network already knows. They helped understand the game, not play it.
Novembre 2026 : une première couche du N: November 2026: a first NNUE layer of 512 neurons instead of 1024. It computes 30 % more nodes per second, but loses 34 to 52 Elo: accuracy matters more than speed.
Une idée n'est bonne qu'une fois mesurée: An idea is only good once measured in games. A better validation error, or a faster program, does not always give a stronger AI: here, only thousands of games on the cluster settled it.
